chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: The tour with Benny Carter
summary: They covered twenty-three states on one-nighters in six weeks; local families opened their homes to musicians.

blocks.x: Okay. Now the other thing is the tour with Benny Carter.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Now I think you told me on the tape that you started in the middle of the summer?
It was '42 I believe. It might have been '41.
Okay, and you went for thirty weeks?

We covered twenty-three states in six weeks on one-nighters. We went as far south as Orlando, Florida and as far west as Texas or Mississippi. Yeah, we played in Dallas, and San Antonio, Texas, Natchez, Shreveport, Mississippi, Louisiana, Alabama. We did a lot of running aroung in those six weeks. That was my first experience on the road with a band, you know, doing one-nighters. I often wondered how singers like Billie Holiday and some of the others, Ella Fitzgerald managed these one-nighters because they were on the road all the time, you know, in the bus. It was pretty rough on the road in those days trying to find accomodations and the actual traveling, you know. I understand that earlier in the very early days some bands on the road, the tendancy was that people
